title: Email installation and recovery guarantees
summary: Install, inspect, or recover Email programs and their provider selector. Deployment runs the product-owned file and setup recipe.
use_when: Email programs should be installed, inspected, or recovered.
do_not_use_when: The goal is to prove live account readiness, authorize a message, or recover retained mail history.
outcome: The supplied programs and provider are selected together, or an explicit setup failure.
effects: Copy supplied programs and documentation into retained releases and update owned public paths under installation locks. Preserve other product selectors and separate product data.
authority: Email owns its program installation and provider selector. The operator supplies artifacts and authorizes selection.
success: Owned command and provider selectors follow the supplied release. Installation runs no signature audit, executable probe, or operational-readiness gate.
failure_and_recovery: Refuse foreign public selectors or stale expected-current selections. An instruction failure retains completed file and selector changes for explicit recovery. Recovery selects retained program files and leaves product data unchanged.
privacy: The wrapper extracts only the RESEND_API_KEY fallback from ~/.zshrc and starts the payload in a scrubbed environment. Credential bytes are absent from release artifacts and command arguments.
Explicit private account settings are separately retained. Installation/recovery probes bypass .zshrc and do not load mail credentials or mail content.
does_not_authorize: Remote account provisioning, credential changes, reading mail, sending a validation message, or taking over foreign selectors.

consumers.statement: Current-user macOS operators and installed callers can rely on the documented program selection and wrapper boundaries.

preconditions.statement: Supplied program and provider paths, an intended installation home, and authority to change owned selectors. Installation does not require a validation receipt.

inputs.statement: Absolute binary and bundle paths, optional home and expected-current selection, or one retained release path for recovery.

outputs.statement: Recorded release metadata and selected public paths, or an installation error. Inspection reports metadata without checking artifact integrity.

data_semantics.statement: Program selection is installation state. It establishes neither database integrity nor dependency readiness nor domain success.

identity_and_units.statement: Opaque UUID release IDs name staged files. Product releases, provider contract versions, and application state versions remain distinct. Installation does not compare component versions or artifact hashes.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Inspection reads current selectors and recorded installation metadata. It does not audit retained content or probe a live dependency.

access.statement: The current-user paths are ~/.local/bin/email and ~/.local/bin/email-install. The wrapper preserves stdin and supplies only the credential fallback, HOME, fixed PATH and ordinary shell bookkeeping; explicit private credentials take precedence. Help/version probes bypass shell credential loading.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Product and catalog locks serialize publication with atomic selector updates. Expected-current guards detect changed selection. An instruction failure retains completed file and selector changes for explicit recovery. Recovery reads retained metadata without integrity validation and preserves separate product state.

operational_limits.statement: Installation copies files and performs product-owned setup without running executable probes or native-signature audits. It runs no installer verify command, database integrity check, provider validation, or readiness probe. Explicit ordinary diagnostic commands keep their existing behavior.

Deploy accepts one bounded schema-two recipe request on stdin. The product command owns its setup; the shared executor uses process exit status only. Deployment runs no application execution probe, native-signature audit, maintenance hold, drain, or automatic rollback.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: The installer retains its existing release layout and supported legacy metadata readers. Installer verify and verify-release commands are removed. Program recovery does not restore product data.

reliances.statement: Ordinary committed-candidate delivery uses the Cell CI manager; explicit authorized manual installation uses matching tested artifacts. The manager owns its integration, validation, repair, deployment and outcome-email semantics.
